thread:
ops-bot Incident created: GPU node flapping + containers restarting in gpu-pool-3 — suspected device address faults (CUDA illegal memory access)

eric-oncall I'm on it, grabbing pager. Can someone post recent logs from the node?

maya-ng Pasting kernel traces from gpu-pool-3 (truncated):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568001] device_printf: illegal device address at 0x7f8a3c000000
[ 1234.568120] cuda: illegal memory access (misaligned address) at kernel nv_gpu_ops.c:0x3f2
[ 1234.569000] show_stack+0x20/0x30
[ 1234.569500] task: serving-runtime[4213] pid:4213 comm:serving-runtime
```
Looks like repeated illegal memory access, then container restart loop.

sam-cox How widespread? Is this single node or many?

maya-ng So far only gpu-pool-3 (3 nodes share the tag), but serving-runtime pods on those nodes are restarting and eviction pressure is causing cross-node load transfer. No other pools showing the same signature yet.

lee-eng Observed 5 restarts in 12m for model-server on gpu-pool-3-02, p99 latency jumped to 12s for affected routes. Some 502/503s surfaced for customers hitting large context generation.

eric-oncall Ok: immediate mitigation plan — 1) cordon gpu-pool-3-02 and gpu-pool-3-03, 2) scale up fallback pool (cpu-fallback) and enable degraded routing for heavy-gen customers, 3) drain affected nodes to avoid noisy restarts. Who can handle drain?

maya-ng I'll run drain commands and collect full dmesg + nvml logs. Also enabling kernel-mode debug logs.

ally-support Drafting short status note for impacted customers: "We're investigating intermittent GPU node failures causing elevated latency and errors for heavy generation workloads. No data loss detected. We'll post updates." Want approval before publish.

sam-cox Can we toggle automatic preemption or eviction to stop churn? Maybe temporarily disable preemption for serving-runtime on these nodes.

lee-eng Preemption disabled on those nodes now (kube taint + runtime flag). That should stop pods being force-killed while we triage.

infra-bot Node gpu-pool-3-02 cordoned by maya-ng at 12:17 UTC. Drain in progress.

maya-ng Drain complete on gpu-pool-3-02. Collected nvml logs and heap traces, uploading to /ops/incident/4071234567/ for postmortem.

eric-oncall Good. maya, can you grep for 'unaligned' or 'offset' in kernel logs? We saw similar in past races.

maya-ng Found multiple occurrences of "unaligned pointer" + "attempted pagewalk at offset not 0x0". Also driver stack shows repeated calls into page table walker during eviction. Suspect a race between our memory cgroup reclaim and the driver's pagewalk leading to misaligned device address.

sam-cox If it's a kernel/driver race we should escalate to NVIDIA driver team and also consider live fallback to quantized CPU models for affected customers.

eric-oncall I agree. ally, can you coordinate customer comms and create tickets for the top 10 impacted orgs? Mark severity P2 for now until we know broader impact.

ally-support Creating support tickets and pinging customers with templated message. Also updating status.redwood.ai — draft ready, hold for final wording.

lee-eng We pushed a temporary serving-runtime flag to reduce max batch size per request to lower memory footprint on GPUs; this reduced OOM-like restarts on a canary pod. If stable, we can expand to other nodes.

maya-ng Can we also disable persistent KV cache on the node group to reduce GPU RAM pressure? That should avoid large contiguous allocations that trigger pagewalk corner cases.

eric-oncall Go for it. lee, coordinate rollout of reduced cache and batch size to the entire gpu-pool-3. We need telemetry on restarts and latency.

lee-eng Rolling to gpu-pool-3. Applying new config now.

infra-bot Config change applied to gpu-pool-3 (reduced batch / cache disable). Monitoring.

maya-ng Early signs: restarts dropped from 5 -> 1 in last 10m on the remaining node. Kernel still showing a single illegal access at 12:34 but no container crash following it yet.

eric-oncall That's promising. Next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned, 2) keep preemption off, 3) keep fallback routing enabled, 4) open escalation to driver vendor with kernel traces + nvml logs. I'll create the external escalation ticket.

sam-cox For rollback plan: if the node shows another deviceaddr event with crash we should evacuate and reprovision the instance (reimage) rather than attempt live kernel patch.

maya-ng Agreed — we've collected serial logs and a full memory map from the node. If this recurs we'll reimage.

ally-support Sending status update to customers now: "We've applied mitigations and rerouted heavy requests — you may see degraded performance for large generations. We're investigating root cause and will provide updates every 30 minutes."

eric-oncall Thanks team. I'm handing off to maya for triage duty for the next shift. If anything spikes, page the oncall rotation.

maya-ng Taking over. Summary for postmortem notes: suspected device address misalignment triggered by concurrent memory reclaim and driver pagewalk; mitigations applied: cordon+drain, disable preemption, reduce batch sizes, disable KV cache, enable CPU fallback routing, prepare reimage plan; escalated to driver vendor with logs.

lee-eng Quick note: no evidence of data exfil or storage corruption. Only memory access faults.

ally-support I'll keep tickets updated and follow-up with the top impacted customers after the escalation ticket is acknowledged.

eric-oncall Closing live coordination thread for now — will reopen if node flapping returns. Thanks :thumbsup:

ops-bot Incident status changed to monitoring at 13:05 UTC.
